# Preface {.unnumbered}

This companion follows the slides of **Chapter 3: Semiconductor Science and Light-Emitting Diodes** (Basics of
Optoelectronics, University of Trento) section by section. The slides tell the story; this book lets you **compute it**. Every
figure is made by a few lines of Python that you can unfold ("Show the Python"), copy and modify. The **live panels** (marked
with a blue bar on the left) recompute directly in your browser. They need no installation.

[![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/{{< var github_user >}}/{{< var repo >}}/blob/main/{{< var subdir >}}/notebooks/interactive_explorers.ipynb) &nbsp;Interactive explorers in Google Colab (no installation, Google account needed).

## Where this chapter sits in the course

Chapter 1 described light as a wave and Chapter 2 guided it in fibers. Chapter 3 builds the **source**. It starts from the band
picture of a crystal, counts electrons and holes, assembles a pn junction, and ends with the light-emitting diode: its
spectrum, its efficiency and how fast it can be switched. The same physics (bands, quasi-Fermi levels, injection,
recombination) is the basis of laser diodes (Ch. 4) and photodetectors (Ch. 5), which are pn junctions run in the other
direction.

::: {.callout-note}
## Units in the code
The slides quote concentrations in cm$^{-3}$ and mobilities in cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$, as most semiconductor texts do. The
code works in **SI units** (m$^{-3}$, m$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$) to avoid factor-of-$10^6$ mistakes in $\varepsilon$, $e$ and
$h$. Energies are in **eV**. Two constants convert: `sl.CM3 = 1e6` (cm$^{-3}$ → m$^{-3}$) and `sl.CM2 = 1e-4`
(cm$^2$ → m$^2$). At 300 K, $k_BT = 25.85$ meV.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}

slide 3 onwards.

## Using the code

All functions live in a small, readable module, [`semilib.py`](semilib.py), which you can import from your own notebooks:

```python
import semilib as sl
sl.carriers(1e16*sl.CM3, 0, sl.MATERIALS["Si"]["ni"])   # n, p of n-type Si (m^-3)
sl.qw_finite(12e-9, 0.30, 0.067)                        # bound levels of a GaAs quantum well (eV)
```

See the appendix [Running the notebooks](running.qmd) for installation.
